rawFindings.title: Nested middleware arrays starting with an empty array are now misclassified as a path
rawFindings.explanation: This broader path-detection condition treats any non-function first leaf as a mount path. For a valid middleware array such as `app.use([[], mw])`, the first leaf after unwrapping is an empty array, so the whole first argument is treated as the path and skipped from the middleware list, leaving no middleware functions to register.
rawFindings.suggestion: Keep the previous empty-array disambiguation while special-casing empty string paths, e.g. `if (typeof arg !== 'function' && (arg === '' || arg == null || arg.length !== 0)) { ... }`.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Calling `app.use([[], function (req, res) { res.end('ok') }])` now throws `TypeError: app.use() requires middleware functions` during setup instead of registering the middleware and responding `ok` to `GET /`.
